segments.sensitive: One reviewer with very sensitive skin reports no irritation, dryness, or breakouts, and finds it gentle enough for nightly makeup removal; other reviewers report eye stinging without specifying a general sensitivity type.
segments.dry: One reviewer uses it on dry skin with a dry cotton pad and reports it removes makeup and sunscreen without stripping, unlike other cleansers she found overdrying.

concerns.barrier: Two reviewers report the product does not strip or dry out their skin and preserves the skin barrier when used dry; several others report a greasy, film-like residue left behind that some feel undermines the skin rather than protecting it.
concerns.dehydration: Reviewers who used it dry as directed report it does not dry out skin and even feels moisturizing; others who rinsed or wiped incorrectly report a filmy, non-cleansed feeling rather than dehydration.

aspects.libelle: Requires double cleansing to feel clean

extraits.texte: I knew better than to cheat on my ride-or-die, Clinique Take the Day Off Balm. That product removes ALL my makeup except sometimes the most stubborn eyeliner. It doesn't sting my eyes either. I love Cerave and was excited to try this. It doesn't remove eye makeup very well at all. I need a second eye makeup remover. It also stings my eyes if I get it in my eyes, so I would have needed a second product to remove eye makeup for that reason as well. I don't lie, the "water" texture it turns into either. It does "ok" on face makeup, but I definitely need to do a second cleanse to make sure all my makeup is off.

Be aware that this does not truly "melt" or rinse off as easily as a cleansing balm like I had hoped. I liked the form factor for shower use for face double cleanse rather than having to screw off a top and dip my finger in a balm container. But this left a petrolatum-like residue on the face that did not rinse cleanly or easily. The residue came off with use of face cleanser, so it may suit some people but I didn't care for it.

Honeslty im very disappointed in CeraVe for this one. It removed most of my face makeup, and didnt feel stripping to my skin, but left a greasy film when i tried to rinse it off. (I know the directions say to wipe it off, but a good product product shouldn't lose that much efficacy if i rinse vs wipe). In my eyes, it stung. And it didnt remove my mascara very well. I use ultra hold Japanese mascara, to be fair, but again that shouldnt be a problem for a genuinely good product. I'm sticking to my other makeup remover, the Neutrogena makeup remover. At least i tried it, but there are much better makeup removers out there. CeraVe can do better

YALL READ THE PRODUCT DIRECTIONS 😭 use this DRY on your face and remove DRY with a towel or cotton round. If you attempt to use water it will work against you as it is oil based. It removed the most difficult waterproof mascara and left a perfect base for my face wash + rinse step. I never leave reviews, but as someone that HATES conventional makeup removers (micellar water burns me, neutrogena is soooo oily and filmy) this gets nothing but a perfect ten from me.

extraits.titre: Did wonders for my skin barrier
extraits.texte: I use this on dry skin and wipe off with a dry cotton pad and it does a great job of removing makeup and sunscreen without stripping my skin. I didn't realize how over drying my other cleansers were. Be sure to follow the instructions because it will not work with water. I personally love that I can use this dry and don't have to worry about washing my face before bed!

This product has been life changing for me! It has helped me with the one thing that keeps me from being consistent with a skin care routine, taking sunscreen and makeup off EVERY night. Yes, some products do a better job leaving my face feeling fully cleansed, BUT they involve water and standing at my sink, both of which I hate most of the time. This requires neither! This is great for disabled people, traveling, camping, the list goes on. I have very sensitive skin and this has never irritated my skin, dried it out, or caused breakouts; and it does a good job cleaning my face until I can give it a more thorough wash in the shower. The only down side is it can leave a little bit of a film if you don't spend enough time wiping it off, and do NOT use water.

I'll admit, I don't follow the directions. I use this as a makeup remover only, then rinse, then follow with cleanser. I love it like this. It melts my mascara off with ease. It really breaks down my makeup well and it doesn't dry me out. I've never experienced burning eyes or anything like that. I think if I used it as instructed, I wouldn't like it thought because it does leave a film, probably to moisturize so you only need one step.
